Version 0.70
Bug Fix: main window is no longer drawn, hidden, and moved when app is launched.
Toolbar now has grey background again.
Bug Fix: On Linux (Mint) password prompt dialog was missing the title. Setting shell to null fixed it.
Bug Fix: On Linux (Mint) password prompt dialog was missing the title. Setting shell to null fixed it.
Added logging. Investigating why app doesn't come up maximized after being maximized and closed and re-opened.

Now saves/restores maximized window state.
One limitation - with multiple monitors, works perfectly on primary monitor. On secondary monitor, works correctly for non-maximized window. For maximized window, restores maximized to primary monitor.
No longer build source code .zip file as source code is in GitHub.

Version 0.97

Version 0.98
User can now specify background of the outline on Linux systems. The Settings dialog / Fonts & Colors tab now allows the user to configure both the outline and the text windows.

Version 0.98
Users can now specify the background color of the outline on Linux systems. The Options / Settings dialog's Fonts & Colors tab now allows the user to configure both the outline and the text windows.
Selecting Edit / Set Font, or right-clicking the text pane and selecting Set Font, now allows the user to specify the text foreground color on Linux systems.

Updated on-line help
Got rid of previous and next links on almost every page. Replaced some content with links to the website.

Updated on-line help
Got rid of previous and next links on almost every page. Replaced some content with links to the website.
Updated on-line help.
Code inspection updates to on-line help content.

For VaultDialog subclasses, the code to display a help page when the user clicks F1 has been moved to VaultDialog.
Subclasses only have to implement getHelpPageName if the help page name needs to be different for different situations. For example, AddItemDialog implements getHelpPageName to specify the correct help page, when that dialog is on "add" or "edit" mode.
Version 0.99 - Now using Eclipse v. 4.39 compponents
Version 0.99 - Now using Eclipse v. 4.39 components

Version 1.00
The user can no longer specify the color of an outline item when specifying the font. Reason: If the user specifies the color, the text of that outline item could be invisible on another machine with a different default text background.

Version 1.00
1) Using 4.40 Eclipse components 2) Allow Linux users to specify Dark Mode in Options / Settings / Fonts & Colors. Checking the Dark Mode checkbox will load more visible graphics in toolbar and menu items.

Version 1.00
1) Using 4.40 Eclipse components 2) Allow Linux users to specify whether or not to use dark mode icons in Options / Settings / Fonts & Colors. Checking the Dark Mode checkbox will load more visible graphics in toolbar and menu items.
